Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Does 20 K equal every die location?
Expected answer / misconception: No. It is a lumped estimate.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R4: IEEE EPS HIR 2023, Ch. 20: Thermal Management | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ch20_thermal.pdf
R15: Feng et al., 2024, two-chiplet thermal interaction and cooling | https://doi.org/10.3390/app14188114

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A lumped steady-state temperature rise equals heat flow times total thermal resistance under its assumptions. Trace the visual in order: power; thermal resistance; temperature rise. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic: 8 W through 2.5 K/W gives 20 K; then list the missing spatial hot-spot and transient effects.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R4: IEEE EPS HIR 2023, Ch. 20: Thermal Management | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ch20_thermal.pdf
R15: Feng et al., 2024, two-chiplet thermal interaction and cooling | https://doi.org/10.3390/app14188114

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Synthetic: 8 W through 2.5 K/W gives 20 K; then list the missing spatial hot-spot and transient effects. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
[Sources]
R4: IEEE EPS HIR 2023, Ch. 20: Thermal Management | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/ch20_thermal.pdf
R15: Feng et al., 2024, two-chiplet thermal interaction and cooling | https://doi.org/10.3390/app14188114

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Free thermal strain difference is approximately ΔαΔT for constant coefficients over the range. Trace the visual in order: CTE difference; temperature change; free mismatch. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic: 10 ppm/K difference across 100 K gives 0.001 free mismatch; do not equate it to local joint strain.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
